## Equity Bancshares, Inc. Third Quarter Results Highlighted by Organic Loan Growth and Announced Merger with Lincoln Bancorp


10/14/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 260 KB](https://s203.q4cdn.com/843919082/files/doc_news/Equity-Bancshares-Inc--Third-Quarter-Results-Highlighted-by-Organic-Loan-Growth-and-Announced-Merger-with-Lincoln-Bancorp-2026.pdf)


*EPS of $1.29 and Core EPS of $1.40 Reflects Franchise Earning Power*


WICHITA, Kan.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Equity Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: EQBK) (“Equity”, “the Company,” “we,” “us,” “our”), the Wichita-based holding company of Equity Bank, reported net income of $26.8 million or $1.29 per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Core earnings per diluted share for the quarter was $1.40.


“This quarter our company continued to execute at an exciting level. Earnings were strong, production reached all-time highs and loans grew organically. We are putting teams in place with an aligned mission to deepen and expand customer relationships while providing exceptional service to the communities we serve. The results for the quarter reflect that mission,” said Brad S. Elliott, Chairman and CEO of Equity Bancshares.


“As our teams realized positive operating results in our current footprint, we announced our merger with Lincoln Bancorp, which will add the incredible team members, growing communities and exceptional customers it has been cultivating for 124 years. The approval process is progressing as planned and we look forward to all our teams will accomplish together in 2027 and beyond,” Mr. Elliott continued.


Notable Items:


- Loans ended the period at $5.4 billion, up $39.2 million or an annualized rate of 2.9%. Legacy markets, excluding those acquired through the Frontier and NBC acquisitions, grew at an annualized rate of 11.9%. Loan production for the period was $379.3 million, up 20.3% quarter over quarter.
- Net interest income was $72.8 million, down $1.0 million quarter over quarter. Growth in interest income of $1.1 million was outpaced by growth in interest expense for the period as deposit costs increased. Year-over-year net interest income was up $10.4 million, or 16.6%. Loan purchase accounting accretion was $3.3 million in the quarter.
- Efficiency ratio for the period was 54.0% compared to 53.4% in the previous period. Non-interest expense, adjusted for merger expenses and intangible amortization, as a percentage of average assets improved 1 basis point quarter over quarter to 2.42%.
- Return on average equity for the quarter was 12.7%, compared to 12.9% in the previous quarter. Return on average tangible common equity ("ROATCE") was 16.1% compared to 16.6% in the previous quarter.
- Book value per share was $39.59 compared to $40.22 in the previous period and tangible book value per share was $32.93 compared to $33.45 in the previous period. Exclusive of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (“AOCI”) book value per share and tangible book value per share increased $1.08 and $1.19, respectively, in the period. Tangible common equity to tangible common assets closed the quarter at 9.1%, up 3 basis points.
- During the quarter, the Company realized net charge-offs of $2.1 million. The allowance for credit losses (“ACL”) closed the quarter at 1.18% of outstanding balances, while ACL plus purchase discounts on loans closed the quarter at 1.65%. As of the end of the period, the ACL was sufficient to cover 7.7 years of current period annualized losses.
- The Company announced a 22% increase in our quarterly dividend to $0.22 on outstanding common shares as of September 30, 2026. Year to date the Company has repurchased 711,369 shares at a weighted average cost of $44.84. As previously announced our repurchase authorization was re-established in September for a total of 1,000,000 shares.


**Financial Results for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026**


Net income was $26.8 million, or $1.29 per diluted share, as compared to $26.4 million, or $1.27 per diluted share in the prior quarter. Core net income was $29.1 million or $1.40 per diluted share, demonstrating the underlying earnings power of the franchise.


The drivers of the current period results are discussed in detail in the following sections.


**Net Interest Income**


Net interest income was $72.8 million for the period, as compared to $73.9 million in the previous quarter. Net interest margin was 4.20%. The decline in net interest income is primarily attributable to an expanding cost of funds and declining yield on earning assets. During the quarter, average earning assets increased $78.0 million driven by investment balances funded by borrowings further driving decline in margin.


Period-end loan balances are $50.4 million higher than average balances during the period. This compositional shift in average earning assets coupled with the full period impact of the FOMC’s decision to raise interest rates in September, is expected to offset deposit pricing competition and yield a return to previous margin expectations of 4.25-4.35% for the fourth quarter, absent the impact of Lincoln.


**Provision for Credit Losses**


During the quarter, the Company recognized a provision for credit losses of $1.7 million, up $353 thousand from the previous quarter. Net charge-offs were $2.1 million, or an annualized 15 basis points of average loans. At quarter end, ACL to gross loans held for investment was 1.18% and ACL plus purchase discounts was 1.65%. ACL levels were sufficient to cover 7.7 years of current period annualized charge-offs as of the end of the period.


The Company continues to estimate the allowance with assumptions reflecting slower prepayment rates and continued disruption from trade policy, elevated inflation, and monetary policy pressures.


**Non-Interest Income**


Total non-interest income was $10.9 million, up $2.8 million from the prior quarter. Following adjustment for one-time items in the previous quarter, non-interest income increased by $0.6 million during the period. Period results were driven by growth in service charges and fees, treasury services and debit and credit card income along with expansion in trust and wealth management revenue. Year-over-year non-interest income, exclusive of gains or loss on security sales has increased $2.0 million, or 22.8%. For the fourth quarter, exclusive of the impact of Lincoln, we expect non-interest income to be between $10.0 and $11.0 million.


**Non-Interest Expense**


Total non-interest expense was $48.1 million as compared to $46.9 million for the prior quarter. Excluding merger expenses in both periods, non-interest expense was $47.2 million versus $46.8 million. GAAP non-interest expense to average assets was effectively flat during the period at 2.58%, down from 3.20% in the same period of the prior year. The efficiency ratio for the period was 54.0%. Non-interest expense for the fourth quarter, exclusive of the impact of Lincoln, is expected in the range of $47.0 to $48.0 million.


**Income Tax Expense**


At September 30, 2026, the effective tax rate for the quarter was 21.2% as compared to 21.6% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily attributable to tax benefits from an investment in a new tax credit structure, non-taxable life insurance proceeds, and share-based compensation activity, partially offset by federal provision-to-return adjustments and non-deductible transaction costs. The year-to-date tax rate is 22.0%.


**Loans, Total Assets and Funding**


Loans held for investment were $5.4 billion at period end, increasing $39.2 million during the quarter, an annualized increase of 2.9%. Annualized loan growth within non-acquired markets for the period was 11.9% outpacing the moderating declines in the acquired markets. Total assets closed the quarter at $7.6 billion, a decrease of $134.5 million which is primarily attributable to cash and cash equivalents.


Total deposit balances closed the quarter at $6.2 billion, down $136.4 million as compared to the previous period. The decline is attributable to rate sensitive time and municipal deposit accounts, as well as seasonal outflows for a few large customers.


**Asset Quality**


Nonperforming assets were $75.4 million, or 0.99% of total assets, compared to $66.3 million or 0.86% at prior quarter end. Classified assets to regulatory capital improved 140 basis points in the period, closing the quarter at 10.42%. The Company continues to actively manage credit quality across all markets.


**Capital**


Book capital decreased $11.3 million quarter over quarter to $816.0 million. Tangible book value per share closed at $32.93, down from $33.45 at prior quarter end. Positive earnings performance net of dividends was offset by an increasing AOCI position as market interest rates moved against our investment portfolio. Exclusive of AOCI, book value and tangible book value per share closed the quarter at $41.49 and $34.83, respectively. Tangible common equity to tangible assets inclusive and exclusive of AOCI closed the quarter at 9.10% and 9.58%, respectively. CET1 capital was 12.15%, total risk-based capital was 14.94%, and the leverage ratio was 10.18%. The Company has repurchased 711,369 shares year to date at a weighted average price of $44.84 per share. The dividend payout ratio year to date was 17.3%, within the Company's 10 to 20% target range.


**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to evaluating the Company’s results of operations in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”), management periodically supplements this evaluation with an analysis of certain non-GAAP financial measures that are intended to provide the reader with additional perspectives on operating results, financial condition and performance trends, while facilitating comparisons with the performance of other financial institutions. Non-GAAP financial measures are not a substitute for GAAP measures, rather, they should be read and used in conjunction with the Company’s GAAP financial information.


The efficiency ratio is a common comparable metric used by banks to understand the expense structure relative to total revenue. In other words, for every dollar of total revenue recognized, how much of that dollar is expended. To improve the comparability of the ratio to our peers, non-core items are excluded. To improve transparency and acknowledging that banks are not consistent in their definition of the efficiency ratio, we include our calculation of this non-GAAP measure.


Core net income is a non-GAAP financial measure that management uses to evaluate the Company’s operating performance across periods. We calculate it by adjusting net income allocable to common stockholders, the most directly comparable GAAP measure, to exclude, net of tax, gains and losses on securities transactions, merger-related costs and provisions, and amortization of intangible assets. Management believes core net income, and the per share and return measures derived from it, give investors a clearer view of results from ongoing operations and make comparisons with other financial institutions easier. The aggregate income tax effect of the adjustments is calculated using the statutory federal rate of 21% and shown in the reconciliation in Table 8.


Core return on average assets and core return on average equity are non-GAAP financial measures. We calculate core return on average assets by dividing annualized core net income by average total assets. We calculate core return on average equity by dividing annualized core net income by average stockholders’ equity, adjusted for the average effect of the core adjustments on equity. The most directly comparable GAAP measures are return on average assets and return on average equity, respectively. Management uses these measures to evaluate how effectively the Company generates earnings from its asset base and equity capital, excluding the items described above, and believes they help investors assess performance across periods and relative to other financial institutions. Reconciliations are included in Table 8.


Core earnings per share is a non-GAAP financial measure we calculate by taking core income divided by the applicable share count. This financial measure is used by financial statement users to evaluate the core financial performance of the Company.


Tangible common equity and related measures are non-GAAP financial measures that exclude the impact of intangible assets, net of deferred taxes, and their related amortization. These financial measures are useful for evaluating the performance of a business consistently, whether acquired or developed internally. Return on average tangible common equity is used by management and readers of our financial statements to understand how efficiently the Company is deploying its common equity. Companies that are able to demonstrate more efficient use of common equity are more likely to be viewed favorably by current and prospective investors.


The Company believes that disclosing these non-GAAP financial measures is both useful internally and is expected by our investors and analysts in order to understand the overall performance of the Company. Other companies may calculate and define their non-GAAP financial measures and supplemental data differently. A reconciliation of GAAP financial measures to non-GAAP measures and other performance ratios, as adjusted, are included in Table 8 in the following press release tables.
